title: Login accounts over a shared connection pool
name: Account login repository

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code borrows and returns database connections? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Inside `with db.connection() as conn:` a statement raises an exception. What state is the connection left in?
choices: Committed, then returned to the pool
Rolled back and returned to the pool, and the exception propagates to the caller
Closed and discarded, shrinking the pool by one
Left checked out until the garbage collector reclaims it

questions.prompt: The pool is created with maxconn=10 and a burst of 50 simultaneous logins arrives, each query taking about 200 ms. What do the logins that cannot get a connection experience?
choices: They wait in the pool's queue until one of the 10 connections is free
They are given extra connections up to the database's own limit
They retry automatically after the connect timeout of 3 seconds

questions.prompt: ping() borrows a connection through the pool and is used as a readiness probe. What is the consequence during heavy load?
choices: The probe has its own reserved connection, so it always reports the database state accurately
The probe can fail with the pool saturated even though the database is healthy, so the instance might be marked unready
The probe waits for a free connection, slowing it but never failing
The probe forces a new connection, adding load to the database
